Psychiatric technicians care for patients with mental or emotional disorders under the direction of physicians or other medical staff, monitor and report physical and mental condition, and may take part in rehabilitation and treatment plans. Medication administration and similar operations vary by regional qualifications and institutional authorization.

O*NET 29-2053.00 lists patient care, physical and mental monitoring, reporting to medical staff, and collaboration on rehabilitation and treatment plans; "may administer medication" does not mean every individual has that authority.

entries: Shift handover | Verify medical instructions and patient identity | Confirm qualifications and restrictions.
Care | Support living and treatment activities | Execute per instructions.
Continuous monitoring | Observe physical and mental status and medication responses | Record based on facts.
Treatment collaboration | Take part in rehabilitation plans per instructions | Do not change the plan on your own.
Safety response | Identify self-harm, violence, or emergency risks | Escalate per procedure.
Handover | Explain observations, execution, and items to be verified | Submit to the medical team for review.

paragraphs:
Collaboration | Work with nurses, psychiatrists, technicians, and social workers.
Workplace | Mental health ward or care facility, may include shifts.
Accuracy requirements | Patient identity, time, verbatim statements, behavior, eating, and safety abnormalities must be accurate.
Decision latitude | Follow the care plan and institutional authorization; do not diagnose independently or change treatment.
Scope of responsibility | Failing to report a crisis or improper restraint can affect patient safety and rights.
Time pressure | Abnormal behavior must be reported promptly.

Communication requirements | Respect patients and hand over to nurses based on facts.
Independent work | Daily care can be divided; medical decisions go to authorized personnel.
Abnormal situations | For self-harm, violence, falls, or acute discomfort, seek help per institutional procedures.
When the care plan, patient restrictions, or medication authority is unclear, ask the nurse first; do not add or execute on your own.

On finding an abnormality, first ensure immediate safety and notify the nurse or physician per procedure; do not let the technician make medical judgments alone.

description.text: Psychiatric technicians care for patients, monitor physical and mental status, and take part in rehabilitation and treatment plans under medical direction. See O*NET 29-2053 tasks, US 2025 wages, BLS 2025–2035 projections, and the qualification boundaries.

subject.name: Psychiatric Technicians
subject.summary: Psychiatric technicians care for patients with mental or emotional disorders under the direction of physicians or other medical staff, observe physical and mental condition, record and report abnormalities, and may take part in rehabilitation and treatment plans. Actual medication administration and other high-risk operations require verifying individual qualifications and institutional authorization.
